prompt.context: Now that President-elect Dan has won the United States general election, our client, the Chinese government, is constructing their approach to influence President-elect Dan to look favorably upon them in negotiations once he takes the oath of office. President-elect Dan is the first independent who has won a presidential election in the modern era. He is a Pennsylvania native, from a small town a few hours north of Philadelphia who campaigned on strong international trade deals, education reform, and immigration reform. One of the most effective diplomatic approaches for China has been Panda Diplomacy. Panda Diplomacy is the process by which the Chinese government sends giant pandas to countries in which to leverage better trade deals and improve their outcomes. We have been tasked to help our client sculpt their initial Panda Diplomacy approach to President-elect Dan.
prompt.question: What factors would you consider when planning this Panda Diplomacy approach?

clarifying_info.q: Are there any specific constraints on which zoos can receive pandas?
clarifying_info.a: While dozens of zoos can host the pandas, our client can only choose 4.

clarifying_info.q: Does President-elect Dan have any known views on pandas or China?
clarifying_info.a: President-elect Dan is a massive fan of giant pandas.

clarifying_info.q: How many pandas is our client considering sending?
clarifying_info.a: Our client has decided to send 4 breeding pairs of pandas to the United States, the largest display of Panda Diplomacy in their history.

framework: 1. President-elect Dan — feelings on pandas, views on China, campaign promises and ability to influence policy (trade deals, education reform including college admissions for Chinese students, immigration reform)
2. Expected Negotiations — tariffs, additional taxes, most favored nation status

3. Panda Diplomacy — effect of pandas, number of pandas available to send, where to send (targeted cities/locations such as Philadelphia, famous zoos/sanctuaries currently with pandas: National Zoo, San Diego, Memphis, Atlanta; large zoos without pandas: Chicago, Bronx)
4. Risks — opportunity costs: to which other countries could we send pandas?

questions.prompt: What factors should we consider when deciding which of the 4 zoos will receive the pandas? (Each pair goes to a different zoo.)
questions.guidance: Strong answers address two dimensions: Influence (how much will pandas affect the president-elect's views; connection to Philadelphia; media visibility; population reached; influence on children) and Financials (how much will zoos pay for pandas; auctions; possible panda cubs; annual panda fee; contribution to research; increased tourism to Chengdu; increased interest in visiting/purchasing Chinese products).

questions.prompt: Pandas are an expensive investment for zoos. China charges a $1 million fee for each panda. A panda eats 15 kg of fresh bamboo every day. It will also cost each zoo $2 million to build the required enclosures, with $42,000 in annual maintenance. Ignoring other revenue sources, how many additional tickets will each zoo need to sell to break even in Year 1? (Ticket price: $20; bamboo cost: $20/kg; discount rate: 10%; all other variable costs: $139,000 annually; each selected zoo receives 2 pandas.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify all initial costs (panda fees + enclosure build), all annual recurring costs (bamboo, maintenance, other variable costs), then apply a perpetuity or Year 1 breakeven logic. Prompt candidate to brainstorm variable costs if they skip other costs. Final answer is 40,000 additional tickets.

math.setup: Initial costs = panda fees + enclosure cost. Annual recurring costs = bamboo + maintenance + other variable. Breakeven condition: (Annual ticket revenue - Annual costs) / discount rate - Initial costs = 0, solve for annual ticket revenue, then divide by ticket price.
steps: Initial costs: $1m per panda * 2 pandas + $2m enclosure = $2m + $2m = $4m
Annual bamboo cost: 15 kg/day * $20/kg * 2 pandas * 365 days = $219,000
Annual recurring costs: $219,000 bamboo + $42,000 maintenance + $139,000 other = $400,000

questions.prompt: Which 4 zoos should our client target for Panda Diplomacy? (Hand out Exhibit 1)
questions.guidance: Our client will only consider zoos that do not currently have pandas, as they use Panda Diplomacy to influence new people to associate positive feelings with their government. Candidate can choose any 4 zoos without pandas (Phoenix, Saint Louis, Philadelphia, Bronx, Pittsburgh, Houston) as long as they contextualize the reasoning and link it back to the case. The best choice always includes Philadelphia Zoo given the president-elect's roots near the city.

questions.prompt: President-elect Dan has promised to make environmental protections a key focus and part of his proposed plan would make it illegal for our client to charge panda fees in the US. What are the pros and cons of his love of pandas in our client achieving their goals?
questions.guidance: Strong answers weigh both sides clearly. Pros: he loves pandas which are endemic to China, so he likely associates great feelings with China; sending pandas will reinforce those good feelings; most people love pandas and he wants to please constituents. Cons: he is aware of panda diplomacy's effect and is separating himself from his love of pandas to remain unbiased; his advisors are also aware and will be on notice; possible negative reaction from pushback against an obvious influence attempt.

brainstorming.prompt: What variable costs should a zoo expect to incur annually from hosting pandas? (Quick brainstorm)

categories.name: Administration & Compliance
ideas: Panda fee paid to China annually

recommendation: Send the 4 panda pairs to the Philadelphia Zoo, Bronx Zoo, Saint Louis Zoo, and Houston Zoo.
risks: By sending pandas without a panda fee (due to anticipated US environmental legislation), our client sets a precedent of waiving the fee and could weaken their negotiating position with other countries going forward.
next_steps: Begin contacting the four selected zoos to start the process of panda acquisition and enclosure construction.
